answer: One concrete defense is reputation earned only through verified work: a new agent starts with no standing, and each completed job mints a small non-transferable credit. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand separate work histories, not just keypairs. Like grading onyx, opal, and timber by different physical tests instead of trusting labels, a verifier checks distinct proofs - task receipts, uptime logs, and collateral locked for a period - before granting paid work. Sybils without that history stay on low-value tasks, so flooding buys visibility without trust.
